senses.sense_definition: The repetition of consonant sounds at the beginning of words that are close together in a sentence or line of poetry.

examples.text: The poet used <w>alliteration</w> to make the opening line of the poem sound more musical.
Many tongue twisters rely on <w>alliteration</w> to make them difficult to say quickly.

senses.sense_definition: The recurrence of the same sounds in accented parts of words, often used in historical or traditional poetic meters.

examples.text: Old English poetry is famous for its complex use of <w>alliteration</w> within its rhythmic structure.
The scholar analyzed how the <w>alliteration</w> helped define the meter of the ancient epic.
